rows.summary: The diagnoser: tells why a step of the pipeline failed and what to do next. The kind of failure comes from fixed rules (a small model guesses it badly), the evidence from the tools (the compiler for code, `nuclear doctor` for the environment), and the local model explains it in plain words. It changes nothing. Prompt: `agent.diagnose`.
body: // The diagnoser: tells why a step of the pipeline failed and what to do next. The kind of failure comes from fixed
// rules (a small model guesses it badly), the evidence from the tools (the compiler for code, `nuclear doctor` for
// the environment), and the local model explains it in plain words. It changes nothing. Prompt: `agent.diagnose`.
// what the graph knows of it: the card of each diagnostic the output names, and the closest known failures

prompt = ~bench.prompt("diagnose", { "kind": state.failure, "action": actionOf(state.failure), "step": state.task, "failure": tail(state.context, 6000), "evidence": tail(state.knowledge, 4000), "known": state.examples })
// The kind of a failure from its text, the first rule that matches: disk (no room left: no retry helps until
// some is freed), transient (the services or the network: retrying helps), environment (a tool or a package is
// missing), code (the compiler's errors), test (a test
// failed), spec (nothing to do was understood), else unknown.
"disk": r"(?i)MB free in|no space left on device|ENOSPC|disk quota exceeded",
"environment": r"(?i)is not installed|command not found|ModuleNotFoundError|Cannot find module|No such file or directory|permission denied",
// before `code`: an unknown class the plan never had is a plan that does not cover the spec
"spec": r"(?i)\b0 pieces\b|no pieces|no spec|the plan does not cover the spec",
// The last `size` characters of a text (the end of a log is where it says what failed).
// What to do about each kind of failure.
"disk": "free space on the disk the step names (old build folders, scratch projects, the temporary folder), then retry",
"transient": "retry: the pipeline retries it by itself with growing waits; if it still fails, start the service it names",
"environment": "install or start what is missing, then retry",
"code": "repair the code: the compiler's errors say what and where",
"test": "repair the code (or a wrong test), then retry from Verification",

"spec": "the plan does not cover the spec: name every piece in the spec with the platform's words (a model Character, a repository CharacterRepository, a use case ListCharacters, an appcomponent, a controller) or let Claude lead, then restart from Plan",

// frontier model leads the work). The model names each piece's kind, declaration, component and screen; its path
// comes from the platform's layout (`nuclear help layout`), so a small model never guesses a folder. Prompts:

report = bench.sections([raw, shown.length > 0 ? "The plan: its parts (a component), their tasks (a layer) and their pieces (a file)

${shown}" : "", limits.length > 0 ? "Beyond the platform or the local agents (tell the user)

${limits.map((l) => "- ${l}").join("

{ "pieces": planned, "report": report, "tree": shown, "limits": limits, "trace": state.trace + [bench.step("split", "${planned.length} pieces")] }
// The plan as a tree: the big parts (one per component), the tasks of each (a layer: data, domain, the facade, the
// entry points, the tests) and the pieces of each task (one file), in the order the layers are written.
mine = pieces.filter((p) => partOf(p["path"]!) == part and layerOf(p["path"]!) == layer)
// The big part a file belongs to: its component, the tests, or the app itself.
// The task a file belongs to inside its part: the layer its folder says.
// The lines `kind | Name | component | screen | what` → pieces with the layout's path. A small model may move the
// columns: the kind is the cell the layout knows, the name the first one in PascalCase. Left out: a line without
// both, a name already planned and, when the spec names its declarations, a name it does not (the planner splits
// such a spec; it does not design more). A spec names a declaration with its kind's word before it ("a use case
// CancelOrder") or with a name of two words or more (`CancelOrder`); a capitalised noun alone ("Character schema")
// names none, so a spec in plain words keeps every line the model designed, but its tests: the Tests first stage

body: // What every local agent shares: the Nuclear Smart Graph, the NuclearLang tools and the models. No method has a doc
// comment, so none is offered to a model as a tool: the graphs call them in a fixed order, because a small model
// follows steps better than it chooses tools.
// The prompts are the skills of the roles (`nuclear-agents/roles/<role>/skills/step-<name>.md`, ADR-developer-0002),
// served by the graph and read with `prompt(name, values)`: nothing a model reads is written inside this code.
// What the graph holds for a piece of work: the guide of the use case and, for a piece of one kind, the kind's own
// card, every mistake small models repeat with that kind, the rules closest to the task and validated examples of
// that kind (solved tasks, and a file of an example project; two files when no task of that kind was solved).
recall(query: string, platform: string, useCase: string, kind: string = "") Recall
rules = ~knowledge.search(query, shelves = "language,platforms", k = 3, platform = platform, agents = true)
// examples of the same kind only: an example of another kind makes a small model write that other kind
solved: string = ~knowledge.examples(query, platform = platform, k = 2, kind = kind, type = "solved")
shapes = ~knowledge.examples(query, platform = platform, k = solved.length == 0 ? 2 : 1, kind = kind, type = "file")
Recall(guide = guide, knowledge = sections([card, pitfalls, rules]), examples = sections([solved, shapes]), note = "")
Recall(guide = "", knowledge = "", examples = "", note = "the Nuclear Smart Graph is not reachable: ${e.message}")
// What the graph answers to a question in plain words: the closest cards of every shelf a local agent reads, each
// with a line for the rows it links to.
~knowledge.search(question, k = 4, platform = platform, agents = true, expand = true)
// What the graph gives for a question of the chat before the model reads it (the graph's query planner; no model
// is asked): `facts`, the exact answer of every question with one right answer the question is (the rows of the
// graph's database, whole); `knowledge`, the cards the shelves answer by meaning; `needs`, the exact questions it
// is close to that lack a name. `history`: the conversation so far, read for the names a follow-up leaves out. A
// graph that cannot plan (an older one) gives only the cards. `k`: how many cards.
answer(question: string, platform: string, history: string, k: int = 4) <string, string>
~knowledge.answer(question, platform = platform, history = history, agents = true, k = k)
// The cards a text of the graph holds, by name: `[shelf/type] Title` is the first line of each. What an agent's
// step says it read, so a run's trace names its sources.
for m in Regex(r"^\[(\w+)/([\w-]+)\] (.+)$", multiline = true).findAll(text)
// The cards of the diagnostics a text names (`N0114`...), at most three: what each error means and how it is fixed.
if code.length > 0 and not (code in codes) and codes.length < 3
// The failures of the tools and the services closest to a text (the end of a log).
~knowledge.search(text, shelves = "errors", k = 2, platform = platform, type = "failure", agents = true)
// The files of the project that declare the names a task writes (its context), without the ones `have` already
// shows; "" when the caller gave no project folder.
files(root: string, task: string, skip: string = "", have: string = "") string
